calls.video_title: Why Is Everyone Talking About SK Hynix Stock Right Now? | SKHY Stock Analysis
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY first tracked 21 Nov @ ~$120, FV $254). Conviction upgraded to medium today. Stock down ~$80 from its near-term high and near its 52-week low despite record operating income and margins. October investor update: memory demand growth is significantly exceeding expectations, supply constrained until 2030, 14 long-term customer agreements (3-5 years, price floor/ceiling, deposits) with major CSPs. Forward P/S 2.9 - 'ridiculously cheap'. DCF fair value $253. He is interested in buying SKHY even though he already owns Micron.
calls.base_case: Supply cannot keep pace with demand; long-term agreements lock in visibility and de-risk capacity build-out; demand from agentic AI now, physical AI (driverless cars, robotics) from ~2030-2033 as LLM growth slows.
calls.bull_case: Cloud capex grows 60%+ in 2027 and AI data-centre infrastructure ~40% a year to 2030; the memory shortage extends and SK Hynix re-rates toward its $253 DCF value.
calls.bear_case: Oversupply risk is near zero near-term but rises to low single-digit percent in 2028 and higher in 2029-2031 if too much capacity is built; US regulation could slow data-centre builds.

calls.video_title: Why Is SK Hynix Stock Crashing, and is it a Buying Opportunity? | SKHY Stock Analysis
calls.thesis: BUY first tracked, conviction upgraded low to medium. SK Hynix fell from ~$200 to ~$120 on AI-regulation fears, but Q3 revenue was +32% QoQ / +328% YoY with an 80% operating margin, supply constrained until 2030, and a forward P/E of just 2.9 — a bargain valuation for a business firing on all cylinders.
calls.base_case: Memory supply shortage persists and prices stay elevated; management expects supply constraints until 2030.
calls.bull_case: Cloud capex grows 60%+ in 2027 and AI data-centre infrastructure grows ~40%/yr until 2030, extending the shortage.
calls.bear_case: US AI regulation slows data-centre builds and new capacity from late 2027 compresses margins and memory prices.
